Heldai
HEL-dye
proper noun
Hebrew cheldai, “worldly” or “enduring, lasting,” the Netophathite, captain of the twelfth monthly course of David’s host, also called Heled and Heleb.

Biblical Definition

Heldai the Netophathite was set over the course of the twelfth month in the ordering of David’s army, of four and twenty thousand men, and he was of Othniel, a man of the stock of that first judge of Israel (1Ch 27:15). He is named among the mighty men of David, called Heled the son of Baanah the Netophathite in the Chronicler’s roll and Heleb in the book of Samuel, the same valiant man under the three forms of the name (1Ch 11:30; 2Sa 23:29). His name perhaps signifies “enduring,” a fitting word for the captain of the last month, who held the rear of the year’s long course. The dictionary honours that Heldai, however his name be spelled, served faithfully to the end, taking the twelfth and final month when the year was full and the labour nearly done. There is a comfort here for the saint who must serve to the last, for the captain of the twelfth month is an image of perseverance unto the end, when the race is nearly run and the crown is near. The kingdom of David figures the kingdom of Christ, and they that endure unto the end shall be saved. Heldai the enduring stands as a witness that the LORD honours the soldier who keeps his rank to the closing month, and that he who is faithful unto death shall receive the crown of life from the hand of the greater David.

Webster 1828 Definition

The Netophathite, captain of the twelfth monthly course of David’s host, also called Heled and Heleb.

HELDAI, the Netophathite, one of the mighty men of David, of the stock of Othniel.

He was set over the course of the twelfth month, of four and twenty thousand men.

He is called Heled the son of Baanah in the Chronicler’s roll.

He is called Heleb the son of Baanah in the book of Samuel.

It witnesses to the perseverance of the soldier who serves unto the end.

Key Scripture

1Ch 27:15 — "The twelfth captain for the twelfth month was Heldai the Netophathite, of Othniel: and in his course were twenty and four thousand."

2Sa 23:29 — "Heleb the son of Baanah, a Netophathite, Ittai the son of Ribai out of Gibeah of the children of Benjamin,"

Mat 24:13 — "But he that shall endure unto the end, the same shall be saved."

Rev 2:10 — "be thou faithful unto death, and I will give thee a crown of life."

Modern Corruption

A man of Scripture, not a contested doctrine; he witnesses to the perseverance of the soldier who serves unto the end.

expand to see more

Heldai the Netophathite is a man of the sacred record, and no movement of the present age has troubled itself to redefine him. The dictionary records him that the reader who meets the name under its several forms may know him for one real soldier in a real host, who kept the twelfth and final course of the year under the king.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is perseverance unto the end. He who held the last month of David’s host, the captain of the twelfth course, is a figure of the saint who endures to the close of his race. The believer wearied near the end may remember Heldai the enduring, and take heart that he who shall endure unto the end shall be saved, and he that is faithful unto death shall receive the crown of life from the hand of the greater David.

Hebrew Roots

Perhaps from the Hebrew for “enduring,” Heldai names the captain of the twelfth course of David’s host.

expand to see more

Heldai — Hebrew cheldai, “worldly” or “enduring, lasting.”

He was the Netophathite, of the stock of Othniel.

He is also called Heled and Heleb the son of Baanah.

He was set over the course of the twelfth month, of four and twenty thousand.

He held the last and closing month of the year’s long course.

Usage

"Like Heldai who kept the twelfth month, the saint is honoured who serves faithfully unto the end of his course."

"He that shall endure unto the end, the same shall be saved, and the faithful unto death shall have the crown of life."

"The captain of the last month is a figure of perseverance, when the race is nearly run and the crown is near."
